additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

symptom.disease_info: Binge-Eating Disorder is characterized by recurrent episodes of consuming unusually large amounts of food in a discrete period, accompanied by a sense of loss of control, and followed by marked distress or guilt. Unlike bulimia nervosa, it is not regularly associated with inappropriate compensatory behaviors such as purging, fasting, or excessive exercise. The course is often chronic or relapsing, with onset frequently linked to stress, negative affect, or longstanding issues around weight and body image, and it can occur across a wide range of body sizes. It commonly co-occurs with mood and anxiety disorders and may fluctuate in severity with life stressors, interpersonal difficulties, or health-related concerns.

patient.personality: Aleta is a sharp, socially engaged retired educator with a competitive, highly organized streak, who delights in learning and community projects while occasionally overextending herself and overlooking her own basic needs.
patient.stressor: After her husband’s death three years ago, Aleta slowly rebuilt a full life through choir, book clubs, and leading an intergenerational literacy project, priding herself on staying as active as she was in her working years. However, over the past year several close friends moved away or became less mobile, and her own mild mobility and medication issues made her give up driving at night, forcing her to cut back on evening social activities and shared meals. In response, she poured even more energy into daytime commitments and meticulous budgeting for her programs, often skipping or delaying meals while out and then eating quickly and alone when she finally got home, treating food as an afterthought until she realized she was routinely finishing entire portions before noticing she was full. Over about five months this hurried, solitary eating pattern became a source of distress and self-criticism, and she sought psychiatric help after her daughter expressed concern that Aleta seemed preoccupied with her eating habits and was "rushing through" meals in a way that didn’t match her otherwise careful, deliberate nature.
patient.chief_complaint: Lately I find myself eating my meals much faster than I intend to, almost like I’m racing through them without meaning to.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: More and more, I come home after a full day at the literacy center and realize I've eaten an entire family-sized frozen casserole or half a loaf of bread with cheese before I even think, 'This is enough for two or three people, not just me.'

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start in on the food, it's as if some switch gets flipped and I keep going, telling myself I should stop but watching my hands keep reaching for another slice or another spoonful anyway, like I'm on autopilot until the plate is bare.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
S051.manifestation: My daughter pointed out the other day that I finished my whole plate before she’d taken three bites, and I’ve noticed that at home I’m practically shoveling food in—barely chewing, barely tasting—just racing through the meal without meaning to.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: There have been many evenings where I’ve eaten so much, so quickly, that I end up sitting in my recliner with my waistband cutting into my stomach, feeling bloated and uncomfortable and thinking, 'If I’d just paused halfway through, I wouldn’t feel like this.'

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I’ve fallen into this pattern of nibbling politely when I’m with the choir ladies at lunch, then waiting until I’m back in my quiet kitchen to really eat, sometimes even standing at the counter or in the pantry so no one, even a neighbor dropping by, sees how much I’m putting away.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
S055.manifestation: After these episodes I often sit there staring at the empty containers, feeling foolish and ashamed—telling myself a woman who can organize grants and run a reading program ought to be able to manage her own dinner plate better than this.
